image_description: A close-up, low-angle shot of a green snake hanging upside down from a branch or vine. The head is facing the viewer, showing a distinct snout and eye. The body curves upwards and out of frame at the top left. The background is a soft, out-of-focus green, suggesting foliage.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape in the image is relatively blunt and rounded at the snout, lacking the distinct 'coffin-shaped' narrowness and prominent brow ridge characteristic of a Green Mamba. It resembles a viper or tree python more than an elapid.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible eye is large, dark, and appears to have a round pupil, consistent with diurnal snakes like the mamba.
The visible portions of the body appear slender and cylindrical/elongated.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is pale yellow-green to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the neck/body visible near the head shows a lighter, yellowish-green coloration compared to the dorsal side.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Due to the angle (hanging down) and lighting, it is difficult to definitively assess lateral compression vs. cylindrical shape. Marked untestable to avoid speculation, though it appears somewhat cylindrical.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The scale pattern on the upper left body segment appears slightly smeared or less defined than the sharp scales on the head, suggesting minor generation inconsistency or focus issues.
The transition from the head to the body has a slight 'melting' quality where the definition of individual scales blurs into the neck muscles, lacking crisp anatomical separation.
